name: Cambodia
tagline: Angkor's ancient temples, the Mekong, quiet beaches and a warm, resilient welcome.
cardDescription: A small country with some of the greatest monuments in Asia, riverside towns, islands and a layered, human history.
metaDescription: A complete Cambodia travel guide: the 10 best places to visit, from Angkor and Siem Reap to Phnom Penh, Kampot and Koh Rong, with practical tips, a two-week itinerary and costs.

image.alt: Angkor Wat and its reflection in a pond

intro: Cambodia is a country of rice fields, rivers and ruins, home to the temples of Angkor, built by the Khmer Empire between the 9th and 15th centuries. The great temples draw most visitors, but the country also has colonial towns, quiet beaches and rural landscapes.

Its modern history includes the horrors of the Khmer Rouge years, which are remembered in memorials in Phnom Penh. Visiting these sites is moving, and Cambodians today are warm, resilient and proud of their culture, with a growing arts scene and tourism industry.

Travel is easy and cheap, with buses connecting main cities and tuk-tuks everywhere. Siem Reap is the usual starting point, then Phnom Penh, with side trips to Battambang, Kampot and the islands. The dry season from November to February is the best time to go.

practicalIntro: The essentials, current for 2026. Cambodia is welcoming and straightforward, but check official sources before travelling.

practical.language: Khmer is the official language. English is widely spoken in tourist areas.
practical.currency: Cambodian riel (KHR) and US dollars both circulate. Around 4,000 riel to the dollar.
practical.money: US dollars are used in cities. ATMs dispense dollars. Carry small notes, and riel for small purchases.
practical.visa: Most nationalities need a visa, available as an e-visa or on arrival. Check current rules and fees.
practical.plugs: Type A, C and G, 230 V, 50 Hz. Bring an adaptor.
practical.emergency: 117 for police, 119 for ambulance, 118 for fire.
practical.tipping: Tipping is not required, but small tips are appreciated for guides and drivers.
practical.safety: Cambodia is generally safe, but watch for bag-snatching from motorbikes and petty theft. Stay on marked paths in rural areas because of unexploded mines, and drink bottled water.
practical.connectivity: Good in cities, patchy in remote areas. SIMs from Cellcard, Smart and Metfone are cheap.
practical.timeZone: Indochina Time (UTC+7), with no daylight saving.

tripDuration.headline: 10-14 days for a first trip

transport.intro: Buses and minivans are cheap and frequent. Flights save time between Siem Reap and Phnom Penh. Tuk-tuks are everywhere.

culture.intro: Cambodians are polite, gentle and respectful of hierarchy and religion. The traditional greeting is the sampeah, palms pressed together, and keeping face matters.

etiquette.title: Dress modestly
etiquette.text: Cover shoulders and knees at temples.

etiquette.title: Keep calm
etiquette.text: Raised voices cause loss of face.
